speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: That fever and respiratory congestion eight weeks ago followed by a month of worsening cough and dyspnea on exertion raises concern for post-infectious complications or an underlying structural issue. Can you describe the nature of your cough more specifically, and have you noticed any wheezing, stridor, or coughing up blood? Additionally, do you have a history of smoking or asthma?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Asthma. The clinical presentation of episodic cough and shortness of breath worsening with exertion and at night, following a recent upper respiratory infection, is classic for post-infectious reactive airway disease or new-onset asthma.
